primary_meaning: In mainstream Christian teaching, 'fruit' primarily symbolizes the visible outward product or evidence of a person's inner spiritual condition — that is, character, conduct, and works that flow from the heart. When applied to believers, it most often refers to Christlike character and good works produced by the Holy Spirit through a life united to Christ (the 'fruit of the Spirit'), and it serves as the test by which genuine faith or true versus false teachers are recognized ('by their fruits you shall know them').
primary_basis: Galatians 5:22-23 (the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, etc.)
Matthew 7:15-20 (a tree is known by its fruit; test of true and false prophets)
John 15:1-8, 16 (the vine and the branches; abiding in Christ to bear much fruit)
Matthew 3:8 / Luke 3:8 (bear fruit worthy of repentance)
Matthew 12:33-35 (the good tree brings forth good fruit out of the heart)
Psalm 1:3 (the righteous like a tree yielding fruit in season)
Colossians 1:10 (bearing fruit in every good work)
Ephesians 5:9 (the fruit of light in goodness, righteousness, and truth)
Matthew 13:23 (the good soil that bears fruit in the parable of the sower)
Philippians 1:11 (filled with the fruit of righteousness)

alternatives.meaning: Converts or evangelistic results — new believers won through gospel ministry are described as 'fruit' of a person's labor.
basis: Romans 1:13 ('that I might have some fruit among you')
John 4:35-36 (gathering fruit for eternal life in the harvest)
1 Corinthians 16:15 (household of Stephanas as 'firstfruits of Achaia')
Colossians 1:6 (the gospel bearing fruit and growing in all the world)

alternatives.meaning: Offspring or children — 'fruit of the womb' as a literal-symbolic idiom for progeny and, in Messianic usage, for the promised descendant.
basis: Psalm 127:3 (the fruit of the womb is a reward)
Genesis 1:28 (be fruitful and multiply)
Deuteronomy 28:4 (blessed shall be the fruit of your womb)
Luke 1:42 (blessed is the fruit of your womb, spoken of Jesus)
Acts 2:30 (the fruit of David's loins on his throne)

alternatives.meaning: Praise, worship, and confession — the 'fruit of the lips' as spoken offering to God.
basis: Hebrews 13:15 (the fruit of lips that confess his name)
Hosea 14:2 (the fruit/offering of our lips)
Isaiah 57:19 (I create the fruit of the lips)

alternatives.meaning: Material provision or financial giving — offerings and shared resources described as fruit.
basis: Romans 15:28 (sealing to them this fruit, the collection for Jerusalem)
Philippians 4:17 (the fruit that increases to your credit)
2 Timothy 2:6 (the hardworking farmer should be first to partake of the fruit)

alternatives.meaning: The consequences or results of actions generally, whether good or evil — a moral cause-and-effect idiom ('fruit of their ways', 'fruit of the wicked').
basis: Proverbs 1:31 (eat the fruit of their way)
Jeremiah 17:10 (to give every man according to the fruit of his doings)
Isaiah 3:10 (the righteous shall eat the fruit of their deeds)
Hosea 10:13 (you have eaten the fruit of lies)

alternatives.meaning: The forbidden fruit of Eden as a symbol of temptation, disobedience, and the fall — sometimes generalized into 'fruit' representing sin's enticement.
basis: Genesis 2:16-17; 3:1-6 (the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil)

alternatives.meaning: Firstfruits as a distinct typological symbol — Christ's resurrection and the Spirit's initial work as pledge or guarantee of the full harvest to come.
basis: 1 Corinthians 15:20, 23 (Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep)
Romans 8:23 (the firstfruits of the Spirit)
James 1:18 (a kind of firstfruits of his creatures)
Leviticus 23:9-14 (the wave offering of firstfruits)

notes: There is a strong, widely recognizable consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions that 'fruit' symbolizes the visible product of a person's inner life — character, works, and Spirit-produced virtues — anchored above all in Galatians 5, Matthew 7, and John 15. Debates exist within that consensus (e.g., whether 'fruit' in John 15 emphasizes character, converts, or obedience; whether fruit-bearing is evidence of salvation or a measure of reward), but these are variations on the same core meaning rather than rival symbols. The alternative senses listed (converts, offspring, praise, giving, firstfruits typology) are context-specific extensions that commentators broadly acknowledge alongside the primary meaning.
